JUDGMENT
The petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

02. The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that, on 28.09.2021 at about 4.00 p.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-05-V-4160 near Narayanareddi House, D.Hosahalli village, Anugondanahalli hobli, Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg No. KA-03-AE-5702 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner, due to which he sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to RKB Sanjeevini Hospital, Bengaluru,
for first aid, thereafter, he was shifted to Manipal hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery for the injuries sustained by him and spent huge amount towards medicine and conveyance.

It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to the accident, he is unable to work and as Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
2 such, he has sustained loss of earnings and he is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.
It is further stated in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AE- 5702, and as such, the police attached to Anugondanahalli Police station have filed FIR against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent being the owner, 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AE-5702 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
03. Inspite of service of summons, the 1st respondent remained absent and hence he was placed as Exparte.
On service of summons, 2nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
04. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of commercial vehicle package policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg No. KA-03-AE-5702 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent has further stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Further this respondent has denied the manner of accident, age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It is also contended that there is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint.
The alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.

Among other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.
05.

On the above pleadings, this court has framed issues as follows:
1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 28.09.2021 at about 4.00 p.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA- 05-V-4160 near Narayanareddi House, D.Hosahalli village, Anugondanahalli hobli, Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg No. KA- 03-AE-5702 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner, due to which he sustained injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioner entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3) What Order or Award?
06.
In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and produced documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to P17.

Also got examined three witnesses as Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
3 PW.2 to PW.4 and they got marked Ex.P18 to 29 documents and closed their side of evidence.

sentences.text: 07. When the case was posted for respondent evidence, the respondents have not lead their evidence.

08. Heard arguments.
09.

The claim of the petitioner is that on 28.09.2021 at about 4.00 p.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-05-V-4160 near Narayanareddi House, D.Hosahalli village, Anugondanahalli hobli, Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg No. KA-03-AE-5702 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner, due to which he sustained injuries.
11.
The petitioner in order to prove the issue examined himself as PW.1 by filing affidavit as his examination in chief and produced documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.

12. Ex.P1 is the true copy of FIR, Ex.P2 is the true copy of first information, Ex.P3 is the statement given by petitioner, Ex.P4 is the true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P5 is the true copy of IMV report,
Ex.P6 is the true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the true copy of charge sheet, Ex.P8 is the discharge summary, Ex.P9 is the driving licence of the petitioner, Ex.P10 is the medical bills, Ex.P11 to 16 are the photos and Ex.P17 is the CD.

PW.2 to 4 produced 12 documents which are marked at Ex.P18 to 29.
13.
The first information was given by the cousin of the petitioner on 02.10.2021 and the accident was occurred on 28.09.2021 after 4 days delay.
On the basis of the information the police attached to the Anugondanahalli PS registered FIR for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
The petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 28.09.2021 soon after the accident.

The PW.2 produced MLC register marked as Ex.P19 and police intimation marked as Ex.P20 goes to show that on 28.09.2021 at about 6.25 p.m. the petitioner was admitted to the hospital and the history mentioned in the MLC register is the road traffic accident between two wheeler and four wheeler.
On the same day, the hospital authority issued intimation to the police and Mahadevapura police endorsed the receipt of information on the same day which is reflected in Ex.P20.
Hence, it is the duty of the IO or anybody on his behalf to visit the hospital and to receive the information regarding the alleged accident.
Since the police have not rushed to the hospital, the first informant being the cousin went to the police station on 02.10.2021 and lodged first information.
The petitioner was admitted in the hospital and he was unable to given first information and police have not received the information from him in the hospital.

Hence, the petitioner unable to give first information on Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
4 the date of accident.

sentences.text: The first informant in his information has stated that he engaged in the hospital to look after the petitioner.
The first priority is to look after the petitioner.

The wound certificate discloses that the injury caused to the petitioner is severe, hence all the family members including the first informant were busy in the hospital and hence they have not given first information to the police on the date of accident.
Hence there was delay of 4 days that cannot be doubted.
14. The IMV report marked as Ex.P5 discloses that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicles.
The front bumper of the car at the right side corner pressed inward and front wind shield glass broken.
The crash guard of the motor cycle bent at the right side establishes that there is head on collusion between two vehicles.
The width of the road is 18 feet as could be seen from mahazar marked at Ex.P4 and alleged accident was occurred in the middle of the road.

The respondent has not obtained any favourable answer from the mouth of PW.1 to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero vehicle and there is fault on the part of the petitioner.
The driver of the Bolero is not examined before the court to establish that there is a contributory negligence.
The driver of the Bolero vehicle drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, as such, he was unable to control his vehicle and to apply brake and hit against the petitioner's vehicle.
Hence, there is a sole negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero vehicle.

15. Ex.P7 is the charge sheet wherein the I.O after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle since during the time of investigation he found that there was negligence on part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no evidence before this tribunal that the Investigation Officer in order to help the petitioner filed the false charge sheet against the driver of the Bolero vehicle.

The documents placed before the tribunal coupled with oral evidence establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Bolero vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-03-AE-5702 and petitioner sustained injuries in the said accident.
Hence I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has produced Wound Certificate of RKB Sanjeeva hospital marked at Ex.P6 which goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The cause of injury is due to accident and on the date of the accident itself the petitioner took first aid treatment.
Thereafter he took treatment as in an inpatient at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, from 28.09.2021 to 06.10.2021 and took treatment.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. Pain and Suffering:
Due to the injuries sustained, the petitioner took first aid at RKB Sanjeeva hospital hospital.

Further Ex.P6 Wound certificate issued by the said hospital discloses that the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
 Cut lacerated wound-multiple face over forehead and nasal region with multiple facial bone fracture, lumbar - 2 vertebra burst fracture.
Thereafter, he was admitted as an inpatient at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, from 28.09.2021 to 06.10.2021 and took conservative treatment as per Ex.P10.

In total the Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
5 petitioner obtained treatment as an inpatient for a period of 9 days.

sentences.text: The petitioner was aged about 22 years.
In that age he suffered a lot and he is suffering from pain due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence by considering the age, the nature of injuries and the period of inpatient in the hospital the petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
18. Towards Medical Bills:
The petitioner has produced the medical bills which are marked at Ex.P10 for Rs.7,20,901/-
On perusal of the said bills, it is clear that petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal hospital and took conservative treatment.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,20,901/-
under this head.
19. Towards Food:
The petitioner is a resident of Bengaluru.

He was admitted at Manipal hospital,
Bengaluru.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he had spent some amount towards food.
At the same time, all the restaurants have not provided cash bill.

Hence by taking into consideration of all these aspects the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,800/- (Rs.200/- x 9 days).
20. Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is a resident of Bengaluru and he was admitted at Manipal hospital, Bengaluru.
There is no document before the court that he had spent amount towards conveyance either after discharge or at followup treatment.

However, by taking into consideration of distance from the place of accident to the hospital and from the hospital to his residence and visa- versa the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,000/- towards conveyance.
21. Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner was inpatient for a period of 9 days at Manipal hospital.
He obtained rest for another 51 days.
During this period he was unable to work, as such he sustained loss.
According to the petitioner he was a driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income and occupation.
However, even if he worked as a coolie then he might have earned Rs.450/- per day.
So the income per month is Rs.13,500/-.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.27,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
22. Future Medical Expenses:
The petitioner examined the Doctor as PW.3 and 4 who have assessed the disability, but there is no mention regarding future medical expenses to be incurred by the petitioner.
Hence, he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
23. Disability / Loss of future Happiness: -
Disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the near future.
Permanent disability refers to the residuary in capacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment.
After achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery, which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person inability to perform all the duties and Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
6 functions that he could perform, though he is able to perform some of them and still able to engage in some gainful activity.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment, related activities as a result of the accident.

Petitioner has examined Medical Records officer of Manipal hospital as PW.2 and he has produced authorisation letter, MLC register extract, Police intimation, case sheet,
x- ray, CT Scan and MRI scan as per Ex.P18 to Ex.P24.

Petitioner has examined the doctor who is working as Professor and HOD of department of Dentistry at Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital as PW.3 and he has produced OP Sheet and X-rays as per Ex.P25 and 26.
Petitioner has also examined the doctor who is working as Consultant Neuro-Surgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics as PW.4 and he has produced OPD record, X-ray report and x- rays at Ex.P27 to 29.

24 . PW.3 Dr. Kumaraswamy, who assessed the disability of the petitioner deposed before the court that, the petitioner sustained multiple facial fractures, deporessed right frontal fracture, nasal bone fracture, right maxillary fracture.
Doctor has assessed the disability at 15% in respect of the facial injuries.

25. Further petitioner has examined PW.4 Shailesh A.V. Rao, who assessed the disability of the petitioner deposed before the court that, the petitioner sustained multiple facial laceration and fracture of nasal bones.
CT scan revealed right frontal depressed fracture with extradural hematoma.
He also had burst fracture of L2 vertebra.
He underwent elevation of right frontal depressed fracture and L1-3 pedicle screw fixation.
Also underwent fixation of nasal bone fracture and wound debridment.
PW.4 has assessed spinal injury @ 10% and this disability is pertaining to whole body.
26. In order to award compensation under this head it is mainly depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

In this connection I would like to rely the ruling reported in 2011 ACJ page 1 in between Rajkumar Vs. Ajay kumar, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the tribunal is required to assess the disability on the basis of evidence and what is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.

As stated above,
the petitioner has not proved that he was driver prior to the accident.
27. PW.3 and 4 are not the treated doctors who deposed during the course of cross examination that the fracture is united.
In the fracture there is no any other complication on the x-ray.
The implants planted to the petitioner are permanent.
The PW.3 deposed that the implants are not put to any of the facial injuries.
The treatment given to the petitioner is conservative line of treatment.
The patient can eat boiled food, but unable to eat hard food.
Because of facial injury the petitioner unable to enjoy his future and unable to eat hard food, but due to the facial injury he has not lost any income.

As far as injury to lower back is concerned, the doctor assessed disability to the whole body Solomon Prakash vs Benire E Store Solutions Pvt Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73671083/
7 at 10%, but he has not given the disability to the particular limb.

sentences.text: The petitioner not been able to resume to his earlier work every day because of spinal implants between L1 and L3.
He is unable to do his work continuously, but he requires rest periodically and as such, it affects on his income.
Hence, the disability sustained by the petitioner is taken at 8%.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,33,280/- (13,500 x 12 x 18 x 8/100) under this head.
28. The above amounts/heads is summarized as follows:

 A. Pain and sufferings 50,000.00  B. Medical bills 7,20,901.00  C. Towards food 1,800.00  D. Towards Conveyance 5,000.00  E. Loss during laid down period 27,000.00  F.
Future medical expenses Nil.
G. Loss of future income due to 2,33,280.00
disability
As far as interest is concerned the petitioner is entitled only 6% interest in view of the verdict of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and also the rate of interest of National Banks.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

30. Issue No.3:- In view of the above discussion to issue No.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,37,981/-/-(Rupees Ten Lakhs thirty seven thousand nine hundred and eighty one only) along with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner along with interest and it is directed to deposit the amount within two months.
